title: Movember: Does Checking Yourself Save Lives?
description:
Movember real talk: does checking yourself every month actually save lives? Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in guys 15 to 45, and the good news is over 95% are alive five years later. Cyto breaks it down, live from the 6ix.

The twist: nobody has proven that routine monthly self-checks save lives. The US Preventive Services Task Force (US guidance, not Canadian) recommends against routine screening in guys with no symptoms, and a 2026 review says the evidence isn't strong enough to recommend for or against. But that's not a reason to ignore your body. Know what's normal for you. A lump, swelling, pain or something off? Don't wait, see a doctor. Early detection may mean lighter treatment.

Sources (via PubMed):
Thomas, Malvita & Rovito, Cancer Prev Res 2026 (review) — https://doi.org/10.1158/1940-6207.CAPR-26-0125
Bashi et al., J Pediatr Urol 2026 — https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpurol.2026.106295

See a doctor about any lump, swelling or pain. Not medical advice.
